name: Kiwi before bed

lead: This practice is eating kiwifruit shortly before bed in the hope of better sleep, which adherents link to skin, recovery and a more rested look.

Kiwifruit is about 83 percent water and rich in vitamin C and vitamin K, with carotenoids and fibre. The reference source consulted does not describe a sleep mechanism, and published trials of kiwifruit and self-reported sleep are small; no appearance outcomes have been studied.

paras: People eat a kiwi or two in the hour or so before bed as an easy food swap, usually as part of a broader evening routine.
Kiwifruit allergy, first described in 1981, ranges from oral itching to anaphylaxis, and the enzyme actinidain is an allergen for some people.

angle.text: Some people eat kiwifruit before bed as a food-based sleep aid, hoping for better sleep and a more rested look. Small trials have looked at self-reported sleep; appearance outcomes have not been studied.

lead: Eating kiwifruit before bed is a food-based practice that some people adopt for sleep. Wikipedia's kiwifruit article describes the fruit as about 83% water, rich in vitamin C and vitamin K, and notes allergy risk, but does not discuss sleep effects [1].
Published trials of kiwifruit and self-reported sleep are small, and no appearance outcomes have been studied.

paras: Kiwifruit allergy was first described in 1981 and ranges from localised oral allergy syndrome to life-threatening anaphylaxis; wheezing is the most common severe symptom [1].
No studies found in the sources reviewed for this article.
